title: Overdue Missed-Visit Fees and Small Credits on an Insured Plan of Care
content:
**Billing desk reference — Insured Plan of Care credits.** A further hold is taken from what remains of the credit once every other amount held back from it has been taken off:

- Where the Appointment Series funded by the plan carries an unpaid missed-visit fee balance and the most recent fee on that series was assessed more than the series' fee due days ago, that unpaid fee balance is held until it is settled.
- Where no such overdue fee stands and what remains is the small-credit maximum of **$10.00** or less, all of it is held on the plan.
- Otherwise nothing more is held.

The refundable credit is then what remains after this hold, never below zero. The missed-visit fee balance, the date each fee was assessed and the fee due days are read from the Appointment Series record and its history.

## Decision table

| Unpaid missed-visit fee balance on the series | Most recent fee assessed more than the fee due days ago | What remains of the credit | Held |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | any amount | The unpaid fee balance |
| Yes | No | $10.00 or less | All of what remains |
| Yes | No | more than $10.00 | Nothing more |
| None | — | $10.00 or less | All of what remains |
| None | — | more than $10.00 | Nothing more |

## Hypothetical illustrations (series fee due days of 30)

- Unpaid fee balance $50.00, most recent fee assessed 31 days ago, $120.00 remaining: $50.00 is held and $70.00 remains.
- The same fee assessed 30 days ago (not more than the fee due days), $120.00 remaining: nothing more is held.
- No unpaid fee, $10.00 remaining: all $10.00 stays on the plan. With $10.01 remaining, nothing more is held.
